h1: What permits are required for a swimming pool in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Swimming Pool Permits: Building Approval and Safety Enclosures
description: Review Newton's pool permit requirement and the city's outdoor-pool enclosure rules before planning an in-ground or above-ground pool.
short_answer: Newton requires a building permit before construction, installation, or enlargement of a private swimming pool. The city also requires an outdoor private pool to be enclosed by a fence or wall at least 5 feet high. Electrical, site, drainage, and zoning requirements may apply separately.

facts.text: Newton's private-pool ordinance prohibits starting construction, installation, or enlargement before the Inspectional Services Commissioner issues a building permit.
Newton requires every outdoor private swimming pool to be enclosed by a fence or wall at least 5 feet high, whether or not the pool contains water.
Newton Engineering reviews site plans involving expansions of impervious area, including pools.

qa.q: Does an above-ground pool avoid Newton's pool permit rule?
qa.a: Newton's cited ordinance applies to private swimming pools generally and requires a building permit before construction, installation, or enlargement. Confirm the requirements for the exact pool design with ISD.
